National And Provincial Assemblies (First Elections) Rules 1962
National And Provincial Assemblies
(First Elections) Rules 1962
[Gazette of Pakistan,
Extraordinary, 27th
March 1962]
No. F. 1 (11)/62-ELS. In exercise of the powers conferred by
Article 85 of the National and Provincial
Assemblies (First Elections) Order, 1962, read with Artiele.86 thereof, the
Election Commission is pleased to make the following Rules, namely :
1. Short title and commencement. (1) These irules may be called the National and Provincial Assemblies
(Elections) Rules, 1962.
(2)
They shall come into force at once.
2.
Definitions. In these rules, unless the context otherwise requires
(a)
"Article" means an article of the National and Provincial Assemblies
(First Elections) Order, 1962 ;
(b)
"Form" means a form appended to these rules.;
(c)
"Order" means the National and Provincial Assemblies (First Elections)
Order, 1962. (President's Order No. 4 of 1962)
3. Nomination
paper. Ever nomination
paper under Article 11 shall be in Form I.
4. Deposits. (1) The Returning Officer shall maintain a register in
Form 11 in which he shall enter every deposit received under Article 12.
(2)
In case of cash receipt, the Returning Officer shall issue ,
receipt in Form II1, and arrange to deposit the amount into the Treasury on the
same day, or if it is not possible to do so, on the next working day.
(3)
The Head of Account for purposes of deposit in the Treasury by the candidate or
the Returning Officer, shall be "P-Deposits and advances Part II Deposits
not bearing interest Civil Deposits Deposits in connec tion with
elections."
5. Manner of marking
ballot papers------
(a)
The mark to be put under Article 32 (3) (b) in
the appropriate place provided for the purpose in the ballot paper shall be one
cross mark (X), and no other mark.
(b)
The elector shall mark his ballot paper with a copying pencil or pen to be provided by the presiding officer at the
polling station, and not with any
other pencil or marking aid.
6. Stray ballot paper. If
any ballot paper which has been issued to an elector has not been inserted by him into the ballot box but is found
anywhere else in or near the polling
station shall be cancelled and accounted for as a spoilt ballot paper.
7. Rejection of ballot paper. Before rejecting any ballot paper under Article 37, the
Returning Officer shall allow the candidates and the election agents, whoever
may be present, reasonable opportunity to inspect the ballot paper but shall
not allow them to handle it or any other ballot paper.
8. Counting of votes.-----(1) The
Returning Officer shall maintain a result sheet in Form IV in respect of all
ballot papers counted by him.
(2)
After the count has been completed and entries relating thereof made in Form IV
the Returning Officer shall declare the result.
9. Account of election expenses. (1) The account of election expenses to be kept by all election agent
under Article 22 shall be kept in Part A of Form V, and the account of the
personal expenses of the candidate referred to in Article 51, shall be kept in
Part B of that Form.
(2)
All vouchers shall be kept along with the account of election expenses arranged
according to the date of payment and serially numbered and such serial numbers
shall be entered in the account under column (f) of the account.
(3)
It shall not be necessary to give particulars under column (e) of the account in regard to the
items of expenditure for which vouchers have not been obtained under Article
50.
10. Return of election expenses. The return of election expenses referred to in Article
54 shall also be in Form V.
11. Affidavits. The affidavits referred to
in Article 54 (3) shall be sworn---
(i) by the candidate who is his own
election agent in Form VI ;
(ii)
by the candidate who employs an election agent in Form
VII ; and
(iii)
the election agent in Form VIII.
